headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Your Home Has High Water Pressure
articleBody:
Having water pressure that's too high can feel like a luxury, giving you powerful showers and quick-filling tubs. But trust us, it's a problem you don't want to ignore. Many homeowners make mistakes that lead to bigger issues down the line. With our 25+ years of experience in Goodyear and the West Valley, we've seen the damage unchecked high water pressure can cause. The biggest mistake? Ignoring it completely.

High water pressure isn't just an inconvenience; it can actively shorten the lifespan of your plumbing system and water-using appliances. Forgetting to regularly check your pressure or delaying action can lead to leaky faucets, constantly running toilets, and even prematurely failing water heaters and washing machines. Another common error is attempting to adjust your pressure-reducing valve (PRV) yourself without proper knowledge or tools. You might set it too low, or worse, damage the valve, leading to inconsistent pressure or a completely failed system. Also, don't assume that just because your neighbors have high pressure, yours is fine; every home's system is unique.

Skipping a professional assessment is another misstep. Even if you think you’ve fixed it, you might have just masked a symptom. A professional plumber can accurately measure your pressure, identify if your PRV is working correctly, and recommend the right solution.
